# Spec：Bifrost 模型访问、短期虚拟 Key 与严格积分计费

状态：已批准。用户已确认主体设计，并于 2026-10-14 明确回复“采用 ADR 0004，测试边界确认”。本 Spec 不启动实施或数据清理。

## Problem Statement

OpenBot 用户希望在工作台和获准接入的外部 Bot 中使用统一模型目录、模型选择及积分额度。当前模型凭据和默认计费接线偏部署级，缺少个人与 Bifrost 治理主体的稳定关联、按 Bot 授权隔离的短期 Key，以及覆盖直连请求的共享预留和可靠结算。

仅把积分余额定期写成 Bifrost 预算不能满足严格防超支：原生美元预算自动按周期重置，并只检查已有消费，不提前锁定本次最大成本；并发调用、实时会话、异步任务和未知价格都可能漏计或超支。用户还需要安全撤销授权、查看待结算额度，并在异常后恢复结算。

公司工作台和外部个人模型授权有不同付款账户，接入 Bifrost 必须正确区分；否则同一用户可能被错误扣到另一类余额，或在清理测试数据时丢失公司账务。发布规则已明确采用 ADR 0004：公司余额与个人余额分别归属，不能自动切换付款方或删除应保留的公司记录。

## Solution

OpenBot 管理身份、Bot 登记、用户绑定、模型访问授权、开放范围、积分台账和模型偏好；Bifrost 提供模型供应商接入、能力与美元价格目录、Customer 及虚拟 Key 执行。

个人用户按需关联一个 Bifrost Customer，每个“用户 × Bot 授权”获得独立、默认 15 分钟的虚拟 Key。已认证服务端 Bot 获取地址、模型信息和 Key 后直连 Bifrost。调用供应商前，Bifrost 必须根据可强制的完整成本上限向 OpenBot 原子预留，成功后才执行；结束后可靠、幂等地结算实际费用。同一付款账户的所有调用共享余额，不能为各 Key 复制额度。

第一版覆盖文本、图像、语音、Embedding、实时及异步等能力，逐“供应商 × 模型 × 调用方式”验证价格、用量与上限后启用。用户可选择模型、管理 Bot 授权并查看个人余额与消费；管理员管理接入、开放能力、同步状态及异常结算。未知费用保持预留，不能因超时、Key 过期或客户端断开重新分配。

公司工作台的普通模型调用仍纳入统一网关准入，但付款方由受信业务归属固定为公司账户；外部 Bot 的个人模型授权固定为个人账户。个人 Key 不授予公司资源或业务工具权限。预留、费用、尾差和恢复事件始终归属原付款账户，余额不足不得消费另一账户。历史公司账务按公司设计保留，清理仅限已核实的废弃测试计费数据。

## User Stories

1. As an OpenBot user, I want my model access to map to a stable Bifrost principal, so that my credentials and spending remain attributable to me.
2. As a new user, I want provisioning to happen when I first authorize a Bot or use a model, so that registration alone does not create unused gateway identities.
3. As a user, I want concurrent provisioning attempts to reuse the same principal, so that I do not receive duplicate accounts or budgets.
4. As a user, I want each authorized Bot to receive its own virtual Key, so that I can revoke one Bot without sharing its credential with another.
5. As a user, I want all my personal Bot Keys to share my available credits, so that additional Bots cannot duplicate my spending allowance.
6. As a user, I want short-lived Keys to renew while authorization remains valid, so that I can keep using a Bot without frequent manual reauthorization.
7. As a user, I want to revoke model access immediately, so that an old Key cannot authorize new paid work.
8. As an external Bot user, I want to bind my external identity after logging into OpenBot, so that nobody can claim my credits by submitting my email or user ID.
9. As a user, I want to confirm the Bot and external identity during binding, so that I know which service receives model access.
10. As an administrator, I want to register and authenticate approved server-side Bots, so that arbitrary third-party services cannot obtain user credentials.
11. As a Bot operator, I want an authenticated credential interface to return the gateway address and permitted model information, so that my Bot can call Bifrost for an authorized user.
12. As a user, I want raw Keys to stay out of browser responses, chat messages and ordinary logs, so that using the management interface does not expose my credential.
13. As a user, I want a synchronized catalog of enabled and administrator-approved models, so that I can choose models that are actually available.
14. As a user, I want models filtered by the Bot's supported capabilities, so that I do not select an incompatible model.
15. As a user, I want a default model for each Bot and an override for each conversation, so that different workflows can use different models.
16. As a user, I want an unavailable selected model to produce an explicit error, so that my model and price do not change silently.
17. As an administrator, I want automatic and manual catalog synchronization, so that model capabilities and prices remain current.
18. As an administrator, I want catalog synchronization to preserve my approved model scope, so that a new upstream model is not automatically exposed.
19. As a user, I want stale pricing and unknown cost paths to be unavailable with a reason, so that calls cannot be charged using missing or unreliable information.
20. As a user, I want explicitly free prices distinguished from unknown prices, so that missing data is not treated as a free service.
21. As a user, I want atomic reservations before paid execution, so that simultaneous Bots cannot overspend my credits.
22. As a user, I want the actual charge to use the price and conversion basis fixed at admission, so that an ongoing request is not repriced unexpectedly.
23. As an administrator, I want to configure an explicit positive USD-to-credit conversion rate, so that the deployment does not assume an arbitrary credit value.
24. As a user, I want fractional charges accumulated accurately, so that many small calls do not receive repeated rounding penalties.
25. As a user, I want available, reserved, pending-settlement and consumed credits shown separately, so that I can understand what I can still spend.
26. As a user, I want calls admitted before a Grant expires to settle against their original reservation, so that expiry does not corrupt an ongoing charge.
27. As a user, I want expired unused credits to remain expired after release, so that a cancelled call does not extend a Grant's lifetime.
28. As a user, I want streaming, failed and cancelled calls charged only for reliably established billable usage, so that an error does not create either free consumption or duplicate charges.
29. As a user, I want unknown results to remain pending while they are investigated, so that the same credits cannot fund an unresolved call and a new call simultaneously.
30. As a user, I want retrying the same settlement message to be harmless, so that service recovery does not debit me twice.
31. As a user, I want each actual provider attempt to receive admission, so that retries and fallback cannot bypass my budget or revoked authorization.
32. As a user, I want realtime work reserved in enforceable units, so that the session stops accepting further paid work when credits are insufficient.
33. As a user, I want asynchronous tasks to reserve their full maximum cost before submission, so that background work remains funded after I leave.
34. As a user, I want retrieving an asynchronous result to avoid another charge, so that checking progress does not duplicate task spending.
35. As a user, I want text, image, audio, embedding and other supported capabilities governed by their complete cost dimensions, so that non-token charges are not omitted.
36. As an administrator, I want unbounded tool or provider capabilities disabled, so that additional fees cannot bypass strict admission.
37. As a user, I want personal purchases, rewards and grants credited to my account, so that payment and consumption refer to the same balance.
38. As a user, I want payment callbacks to use persisted order ownership, so that another user cannot redirect my credited purchase.
39. As an administrator, I want Key deletion, disablement and ownership drift detected, so that Bifrost changes cannot silently expand user authorization.
40. As an administrator, I want manually created Keys to remain outside OpenBot authorization until explicitly managed, so that gateway changes cannot bypass credit admission.
41. As an administrator, I want durable settlement retry and recovery after restarts, so that gateway or billing outages do not lose usage or charges.
42. As an administrator, I want evidence-based settlement resolution and audited compensation, so that unknown results are resolved without inventing usage or silently forgiving costs.
43. As a user, I want account or Bot suspension to prevent new execution and attempt cancellation, so that lost authorization limits further spending.
44. As an administrator, I want financial obligations to survive account suspension or deletion, so that pending costs remain recoverable and attributable.
45. As an administrator, I want narrowly scoped cleanup of confirmed obsolete test billing data, so that unrelated users, Bots, conversations and knowledge are preserved.
46. As an administrator, I want clear readiness, synchronization and settlement health information, so that incomplete gateway configuration cannot appear operational.
47. As a user, I want subscription-harness calls clearly distinguished from Bifrost credit calls, so that I understand their billing and credential source.
48. As an account owner, I want spending permanently bound to the authorized payer, so that insufficient credits cannot silently charge another account.
49. As a company user, I want company-workbench model calls charged to the authorized company account, so that switching workspace or personal model settings does not change the payer.
50. As a personal Bot user, I want my personal authorization to use only my personal balance and grant no company-content permission, so that gateway access cannot cross business boundaries.
51. As a company account owner, I want company financial history preserved independently of obsolete test-data cleanup, so that the integration cannot erase or duplicate company funds.

## Implementation Decisions

1. Reuse the existing authenticated identity, credential storage, CreditWriter, Credit Ledger, usage outbox and payment ownership mechanisms. Extend their contracts for the authorized payer and durable gateway consumption rather than creating a second credit ledger.
2. Store stable personal-user-to-Customer mappings and per-user/per-Bot model access grants. Separate the Bot service identity, external identity binding and user's authorization; client-supplied identifiers cannot establish the payer.
3. Manage virtual Key versions beneath a stable authorization. Default lifetime is 15 minutes and configurable; renewal requires current authorization. All active versions must become unusable for new admission when the grant is revoked. Rotation does not reset credits or release outstanding reservations.
4. The server-side credential interface returns a Bifrost endpoint, model information, Key and expiry only to the authenticated Bot acting under a valid user grant. User-facing interfaces return status, expiry and authorization management without the raw secret.
5. Catalog identities include provider, model and invocation capability. Maintain versioned prices, synchronization timestamps and administrator-approved scope. Default synchronization interval is 5 minutes; the default freshness limit is 15 minutes; both are configurable. Unknown pricing is a distinct state from explicit zero pricing.
6. Model preferences resolve from user-global default to user/Bot default to conversation override. Chosen unavailable models fail explicitly; the first release does not switch to another model automatically.
7. Bifrost gateway admission must synchronously obtain a reservation from OpenBot before provider work. Ordinary plugin errors cannot be relied upon to stop execution. No alternative gateway entry, retry, tool path or provider attempt may bypass the same requirement.
8. A reservation commits the payer, authorization, provider/model/capability, enforceable maximum cost, pricing and conversion versions and stable attempt identity. Replayed reserve operations cannot create duplicate holds; uncertain admission responses must be resolved before provider execution.
9. The authenticated settlement contract accepts reliable usage evidence and references the original reservation. Identical replay has one effect; conflicting replay is rejected. Releasing a reservation requires established absence of billable work or a confirmed releasable remainder, not a timeout alone.
10. Reuse transactional account serialization for shared credit admission. Unresolved expired holds remain unavailable to new work. Do not directly inherit legacy hold expiry reclamation or the older empirical token-estimation guarantee as proof of strict bounds.
11. Price and conversion calculations use explicit decimal precision or rational arithmetic. Reserve a sufficient upper bound at the smallest stored unit, accumulate actual fractional remainders per payer, and retain the locked calculation basis. No implicit USD-to-credit ratio is provided.
12. Expand capability admission across text/Responses, embeddings, images, audio, realtime and existing asynchronous/video/batch/tool paths. Each enabled adapter must provide complete pricing, dependable billable usage and an enforceable maximum including cancellation tail costs. Unsupported paths remain visible as unavailable with reasons.
13. Realtime admission and settlement operate per bounded billing unit. A session controller must prevent further paid processing when reservation fails or authorization expires, accounting for any unavoidable tail cost. A per-turn usage check alone is insufficient.
14. Asynchronous and batch submission reserve the complete enforceable job cost; task/attempt records carry immutable payer and reservation ownership. Result retrieval is not a second billable submission. Cancellation without a reliable unbilled terminal result does not free the hold.
15. Persist execution commitments before provider dispatch and durably record results pending acknowledgement. Recovery handles gateway restarts, delivery retries, provider status lookup and unknown outcomes without releasing unresolved credits.
16. Preserve settlement and required attribution after user/Bot suspension or deletion. Separate read-only Reconciliation from evidence-based Settlement Resolution and separately audited platform-funded compensation.
17. All personal grants, rewards, purchase orders and subscriptions use persisted personal ownership; payment callbacks resolve that ownership from server records. Company-workbench calls use the company account fixed by trusted business context, while external personal-authorized Bot calls use the grant's personal account. Persist payer type and identity throughout admission, usage, settlement, remainders and recovery; IDs must not collide or replay between payer types. Neither client-supplied account IDs nor insufficient balance may switch the payer. Individual company-wallet provisioning is owned by the company/team workstream, not a new personal Key granting company access.
18. Reuse existing user billing/Bot screens and administrator settings for balances, pending charges, consumption, model selection, grants, gateway readiness, synchronization and anomaly handling. Unconfigured rates or unverified gateway capability prevent enablement.
19. Known violations of a proven maximum freeze the affected capability and retain evidence. Do not debit into an unexplained negative balance, quietly lower the strict guarantee, or count such a capability as accepted.
20. Preserve company financial history and apply the company design's verified ownership/migration rules. Cleanup is restricted to explicitly inventoried obsolete test billing records; unknown ownership is isolated for investigation rather than guessed or deleted. Do not copy one legacy balance to both personal and company accounts.

## Testing Decisions

Prefer one highest public workflow boundary: a registered Bot obtains credentials under a user authorization and invokes the Bifrost inference interface. Assert externally visible authorization, errors, whether the provider was actually called, payer balance and reported consumption. Add focused database-backed coverage beneath that boundary for atomicity and durable recovery; do not assert private hook call counts or duplicate the implementation's internal structure.

Existing prior art includes CreditWriter PostgreSQL integration tests for keyed grants, concurrent spending and reservations; usage-outbox integration tests for durable replay and partial target delivery; billing route and webhook-signature tests for authorization and callback ownership; Bifrost governance/refusal/concurrency tests and live-meter tests for gateway and realtime behavior. Reuse those harnesses and patterns where applicable; their current presence is not evidence that this new integration passes.

Test modules are the public Bot authorization/credential workflow, Bifrost admission and consumption delivery, account-level credit transactions, versioned catalog/conversion, asynchronous/realtime controllers, payment ownership and the user/admin management screens. Provider fakes make dispatch, uncertainty and billable failures deterministic; actual supplier conformance checks validate the claimed enforceable bounds before enabling an adapter.

| Acceptance | Required observable result |
| --- | --- |
| AC01 | Two users have isolated personal balances; concurrent provisioning creates one effective personal Customer mapping. |
| AC02 | Two Bots have distinct Keys sharing one user's credits; issuing or rotating a Key cannot multiply allowance. |
| AC03 | Binding requires authenticated confirmation; forged user IDs, emails, replayed binding codes and Bot authentication alone cannot claim another user's credentials. |
| AC04 | With balance 10, two concurrent requests each requiring a maximum of 8 result in only one reservation and one provider dispatch. |
| AC05 | Credit-service timeout/unavailability, missing admission enforcement and invalid grants never dispatch provider work; alternate endpoints and attempts cannot bypass admission. |
| AC06 | Missing prices, unreliable usage or unenforceable bounds reject execution with a visible reason; explicit free pricing is separate from unknown pricing. |
| AC07 | Success, streaming completion, billable failures/cancellation, duplicate events and process restarts neither lose nor duplicate charges. |
| AC08 | Default 15-minute expiry and valid-grant renewal work; revoked old Keys cannot start paid work; expiry does not erase outstanding liability. |
| AC09 | Bot defaults and conversation overrides take effect; unavailable selection does not silently switch model. |
| AC10 | Automatic/manual sync respects the default 5/15-minute timing, preserves approved scope and blocks affected stale-price calls without repricing existing reservations. |
| AC11 | Deleted/disabled/drifted Keys are identified; manually created Keys do not acquire OpenBot authorization. |
| AC12 | Missing conversion configuration prevents enablement; changes affect new requests only; repeated small costs accumulate the correct remainder. |
| AC13 | Company-workbench calls retain the trusted company payer and personal-authorized external calls retain the personal payer through admission, usage, settlement and remainder; neither insufficient balance nor workspace switching changes the payer, and personal Keys grant no company-content access. Subscription harnesses cannot become a balance-exhaustion fallback. |
| AC14 | Personal grants, orders, subscriptions and callbacks use personal ownership; another user cannot read, mutate or redirect them. |
| AC15 | A Grant expiring mid-request still settles the admitted work; expired unused remainder stays expired; unknown holds stay unavailable. |
| AC16 | Realtime units reserve before processing and stop subsequent work on exhaustion/revocation; asynchronous tasks retain full reservations and repeated retrieval does not re-charge. |
| AC17 | Unknown-result recovery, alerts and audited evidence-based resolution work; disabling/deleting a user preserves necessary liability. |
| AC18 | Cleanup affects only enumerated and verified obsolete test billing data; users, Bots, conversations, knowledge and company financial history remain intact. Unknown-owner records are isolated; no legacy balance is duplicated into personal and company accounts. |
| AC19 | User/admin screens enforce their respective authorization and do not expose raw Keys in frontend responses, messages or ordinary logs. |

Tests must include time-controlled expiry/freshness, interrupted reserve acknowledgement, interrupted settlement acknowledgement, multi-process account concurrency, provider work admitted before a crash, realtime termination tail costs and asynchronous completion after Key expiry. SQL-backed tests cannot be replaced by in-memory mocks for transaction guarantees. A skipped integration or supplier conformance check is not passing evidence.

## Out of Scope

- Organization/team membership, content isolation and a company-wallet implementation are owned by the separately approved company/team design. This integration must honor the confirmed account routing without silently rewriting that design.
- Arbitrary third-party Bot self-registration, browser delivery of raw Keys and automatically adopting manually created gateway Keys.
- Automatic model substitution, copying a user balance into each Key, or treating a resetting Bifrost budget as the authoritative credit ledger.
- Using empirical estimates, missing-price zero values or periodic budget polling as proof of strict prevention of overspending.
- Routing subscription harness credentials through personal Bifrost Keys or using them as an automatic fallback.
- Cleanup outside the precisely authorized billing-data scope, actual infrastructure provisioning, production deployment or external subscription cancellation as part of this specification publication.
- Production code implementation and ticket creation in this to-spec task; those follow the repository's separate engineering workflow.

## Further Notes

- This specification synthesizes the approved Bifrost design, its 30 decisions and 19 acceptance criteria, the domain glossary and accepted ADR 0002/0003. It preserves comprehensive capability scope; no text-only downgrade is authorized.
- Publication target is `1123786563/OpenBot`, explicitly corrected by the user on 2026-10-15. Apply the existing `ready-for-agent` label without another triage round.
- Cross-Spec resolution is confirmed by the user's “采用 ADR 0004，测试边界确认”: company-workbench/company payer and externally authorized personal-Bot/personal payer remain separate. Preserve company financial history and clean only confirmed obsolete test billing records. This resolution supersedes conflicting blanket personal-payer and legacy-cleanup statements in the original Bifrost interview; other approved decisions remain in effect.
- The user confirmed the public Bot credential-plus-gateway workflow as the main test boundary, supplemented by existing transactional credit integration and recovery tests. Company payer routing must also be exercised at its existing authenticated workbench execution boundary; do not impersonate that business authorization with a personal Key.
- Source inspection verified available gateway routes and extension seams, not deployed provider bounds, pricing correctness or recovery guarantees. Each enabled capability requires supplier-specific evidence and verification at implementation time.
- Strict admission differs from the older accepted empirical input-count policy. Existing older behavior is not silently redefined; the new strict path must either meet its complete guarantee or remain unavailable.
- Subsequent work uses vertical business tickets, then worktree/DAG, writing-plans, subagent-driven-development and complete-range OCR/fix/re-review according to repository guidance. This Issue is the specification source, not permission to skip those gates.
